subject: MSA / Order Form – proposed SLA amendments and maintenance carveouts
messages:
From: Tom Blake <tom.blake@avalon-ops.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@avalon-ops.com>, Rachel Owens <rachel.owens@avalon-ops.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on SLA language in the MSA + Order Form

Hi Sean,

Thanks for sending over the MSA and Order Form. Our procurement and engineering teams flagged a few SLA items that need clarification before we can move to signature:

- The uptime target reads "99.9%" for the hosted service but doesn't define measurement windows or regional fallbacks. We need clarifying language (prefer 99.95% for core production).
- The service credit formula is unclear; procurement needs a cap and an example calculation.
- Maintenance windows: we want explicit limits on planned maintenance per quarter and a guaranteed minimum notice (72 hours).
- Emergency maintenance carveouts — we need an acceptable definition for security/incident-related work and any required notice after-the-fact.

I've attached a short redline from our side (attached). Can you confirm Redwood's flexibility and what your legal team needs to approve these items? If easier, happy to take a short call this week.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Blake
Head of Platform
Avalon Ops

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Tom Blake <tom.blake@avalon-ops.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 10:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on SLA language in the MSA + Order Form

Tom — thanks for the clear note. Appreciate the specificity.

Quick read: we can make progress on all four bullets but will need legal to sign off on caps and precise carveouts. I've put together a short proposed amendment (RWI_proposed_sla_amendments_20260630.docx) that:

- Proposes a two-tier uptime metric: 99.95% for "Dedicated" (reserved capacity) and 99.9% for "Hosted" across a calendar-month measurement window, with region/availability-zone measurement defined in Appendix A.
- Offers a service credit schedule (single-incident credit tiers) and a monthly cap equal to 30% of the monthly invoice for the impacted service. Example calculations are included.
- Defines planned maintenance as up to 4 hours per calendar quarter per region with 72 hours notice; additional scheduled windows are subject to mutual agreement.
- Provides an emergency maintenance carveout for verified security patches or incident remediation with immediate action allowed and a post-action notification within 24 hours.

I'm looping in Lauren and Aditya to coordinate final redlines. If those high-level points look acceptable to you, we'll ask legal to produce an MSA redline and then route to procurement.

Next steps I propose:
1) Lauren: produce formal redline of the MSA + Order Form with the credit cap language and regional measurement definition.
2) Marissa/Aditya: confirm commercial concession (monthly cap) and whether we can keep separate uptime targets for Dedicated vs Hosted.
3) Sean: schedule 30-minute alignment call with Avalon procurement if needed.

I'll attach the proposed amendment now.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: RWI_proposed_sla_amendments_20260630.docx (internal proposed language)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on SLA language in the MSA + Order Form

Thanks — reviewed the proposed amendment. High-level legal comments and requested edits below (I'll produce a tracked redline by EOD):

1) Service credit cap: we are comfortable with a monthly cap but recommend 30% of the monthly invoice for the impacted service (we should avoid unlimited credits). That aligns with our standard practice.

2) Uptime measurement: we prefer a single measurement approach (calendar month, UTC) and tying the SLA to the specific region(s) listed on the Order Form. The proposed two-tier approach is fine commercially, but legal prefers explicit language that the uptime calculation excludes scheduled maintenance and force majeure.

3) Planned maintenance: Accept 4 hours per quarter per region as a baseline, but add language that additional maintenance (e.g., version upgrades) must be scheduled with at least 7 days' notice if it will impact availability beyond a routine window.

4) Emergency maintenance carveout: permitted only for verified security vulnerabilities or critical incident containment. We should require post-event disclosure detailing scope and root cause within 72 hours and provide the customer a one-time contract credit (not additional credits) if the emergency action was within our control and caused measurable downtime beyond the carveout.

5) Example calculations: legal will include an explicit worked example showing how credits apply across multi-region services to avoid interpretation disputes.

Key ask: we need commercial confirmation on the 30% cap and whether sales can accept a differentiation between Dedicated (99.95) and Hosted (99.9). If sales approves, I'll ship the redline to Avalon procurement.

—Lauren
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: (legal will send tracked redline later)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Blake <tom.blake@avalon-ops.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on SLA language in the MSA + Order Form

Tom — thanks for the notes and quick turnaround, Sean & Lauren. Wanted to jump in on the commercial perspective so procurement has clarity before legal redlines land.

From a sales/ops lens we can agree to the following compromise to keep momentum:

- Uptime: Redwood will commit to 99.95% for Dedicated (customers with reserved capacity on the Order Form) and 99.9% for Hosted. Measurement will be calendar-month, UTC and will explicitly exclude scheduled maintenance and force majeure.
- Credits: Service credit schedule will remain tiered (example: 99.0–99.89 => 10% credit, 98.0–98.99 => 25% credit, <98.0 => 50% credit) with a monthly cap at 30% of the monthly invoice for the impacted service. We can't agree to unlimited carry-forward credits.
- Planned maintenance: Standard: up to 4 hours per calendar quarter per region with 72 hours notice. For major upgrades that require >4 hours, Redwood will provide 7 days' notice and offer a one-time operational window outside business hours whenever possible.
- Emergency maintenance: Redwood to act immediately for verified security incidents; we will notify within 24 hours and provide a root-cause follow-up within 72 hours. If our emergency action causes measurable downtime beyond the carveout window due to process failure, we'll offer a one-time goodwill credit (not in addition to the monthly credit cap).

I've attached the latest Order Form (v3) with these points reflected in the commercial section so procurement can see how the changes land on price and commitment. If Avalon can accept the 30% monthly cap, legal can proceed with a tracked MSA redline and we can route to signature.

Proposed immediate step: sign-off on cap and uptime differentiation so Lauren can issue the formal redline. If Avalon needs higher uptime (99.95) for Hosted we can discuss a premium committed spend for that level.

—Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: OrderForm_Avalon_v3.pdf (commercial v3, stub)

From: Tom Blake <tom.blake@avalon-ops.com>

Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on SLA language in the MSA + Order Form

Sean / Marissa / Lauren — thanks for the thoughtful response and the revised commercial framing. A few quick points from Avalon procurement/engineering:

- We appreciate the differentiation for Dedicated vs Hosted. For our core production workloads (multi-region failover), we cannot accept 99.9% for Hosted without additional guarantees. If Redwood will commit to 99.95% on the Order Form for the services that Avalon lists as "production" (we can specify the SKUs), we can proceed to sign. If not, procurement will request a price credit that offsets increased operational risk.
- The 30% monthly cap is acceptable as a starting point, but procurement asks that the definition of "monthly invoice for the impacted service" be explicit in the Order Form (line-item reference).
- Emergency maintenance carveout: agreed on immediate action for security, but we need a stronger post-event disclosure timeline (48 hours preferred) with a remediation plan within 7 days.

Happy to schedule a short call tomorrow to align on the handshake language. If legal needs to escalate, please let us know the fastest path — we aim to sign within two weeks.

Tom
Tom Blake
Head of Platform, Avalon Ops
